title: Pressure ulcers: site, stage and healing
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's pressure ulcer, if any.
note:
Chief Complaint: Sacral pressure ulcer management.

HPI: [Copied Forward] Patient is a 77-year-old female presenting for evaluation of a pressure injury. She reports difficulty with mobility and is primarily bedbound. She reports localized discomfort at the site of the wound.
[Update] Patient returns for a follow-up of her pressure ulcer over the sacrum. She reports that the area remains painful but there have been no new drainage issues. She continues to use a pressure-redistributing mattress.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Vitals: BP 134/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative
Integumentary: Positive (Sacral wound)
Musculoskeletal: Positive (Limited mobility)
All other systems negative.

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears in no acute distress.
Skin: Large pressure ulcer over the sacrum. The wound is unstageable as the wound base is covered by eschar. No surrounding erythema noted.

Assessment:
1. Unstageable pressure ulcer of the sacrum.

Plan:
1. Continue wound care and dressing changes.
2. Maintain pressure-redistributing surface.
3. Follow up in two weeks for reassessment.

Electronically signed,
R. Mensah, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: Pressure ulcer of the sacral region, unstageable (base covered by eschar or slough): L89.150 (HCC 381).

distractors.why: Unstageable is a documented stage (L89.--0), not 'unspecified'.
Do not assign a stage the provider could not determine.

hccs.label: Pressure Ulcer of Skin with Full Thickness Skin Loss
